title: Faint the Earth, and Parched with Drought
description: Faint the Earth, and Parched with Drought in Tonic Solfa to MESSIAH (HERALD), doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 598, “The Prophet's Vision”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MESSIAH (HERALD); any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Faint the earth, and parched with drought, Make the wa-ters, Lord, gush out! Streams of love our thirst to bless, Start-ing in the wild-er-ness. Long we wait Thy peace to know: Fa-ther, bid the wa-ters flow, Make the thirst-y land a pool, Make man's suf-fering spi-rit whole.

lines: Faint the earth, and parched with drought,
Make the waters, Lord, gush out!
Streams of love our thirst to bless,
Long we wait Thy peace to know:
Make the thirsty land a pool,
Hark! the wastes have found a voice;
When the Lord His presence shows,
Lo, they blossom like the rose;
See! this barren earth of ours
Buds and puts forth fruits and flowers,
Flowers of Eden, fruits of peace,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to MESSIAH (HERALD) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
